rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the majority together by writing a narrow opinion rejecting a net-loss requirement while adopting an object-of-the-scheme “economically adverse terms/benefit-of-the-bargain” limiter to avoid a backdoor right-to-control theory. Kagan is the most likely principal dissenter (with possible separate writings from Jackson or Gorsuch) arguing the limiter is atextual and that material deception to obtain traditional money/property suffices under §1343.
